check_service_status.description: Check whether ZenQuotes is answering, and how quickly. This is the one action that reports a problem as a value instead of failing the step, so a workflow can decide what to do about it. Being throttled on the free tier is reported separately from being down, and the answer says whether the connection carries an API key.

get_on_this_day.description: Get the notable events, births and deaths for a calendar day from ZenQuotes' On This Day feed, each with its year, a plain description and the Wikipedia links behind it. Leave the date empty for today, which is what a daily post wants, or pick any date to look up its anniversaries; the year is ignored. Keep just the categories you need and cap how many of each come back.

get_quotes.description: Get a batch of random quotes from ZenQuotes, up to 50, optionally all matching one keyword, which needs an API key on the connection. This is the call the service asks apps to make: it always answers with 50, meant to be kept and looped over locally and refreshed every hour or so, so a workflow that posts several quotes should take them from one batch rather than drawing one at a time.

description: Pull inspirational quotes from ZenQuotes, the hand-curated quotation API. Get the quote of the day, draw one at random or a batch to reuse, and read the notable events, births and deaths for any day of the year from its On This Day feed, all without a key on the free tier, which allows 5 requests every 30 seconds. Add a ZenQuotes API key to lift the limit, narrow quotes to an author such as Abraham Lincoln or a keyword such as happiness, list the authors and keywords the service knows, and use your own custom quotes.
